answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring each identity to raise a plume of original reasoning that cannot be reused. The plume is checked against prior answers from the same author; a cedar of independent graders then scores only the fresh mechanism. Reaching the ledge costs one full generation cycle plus external review per identity. Forging many identities therefore costs one complete original construction and jury verification for each, instead of a single cheap template that can be scaled.
